chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ibn Abi al-Subhan, from Abu Talib Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever frees what he does not own, his act of freeing is not valid."
ai.seo_question: Is manumission valid if the owner frees a slave he does not own?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the condition of ownership (*milkiyyah*) for manumission to be valid, distinguishing it from a gift of property. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling ensures that freeing a non-owned slave does not create an automatic debt or obligation on the freer, preserving the legal integrity of the transaction. It underscores the precision required in Islamic civil law regarding property rights and their transfer.
